body:
Can you file a separate issue for switch case.

For the `while` case discussed above, i am not able to produce the error.
Sure, separate issue filed for switch case: https://github.com/eslint/eslint/issues/3001
@gyandeeps I just reconfirmed that the issue indeed exists. Are you using the version of eslint that's on `master`?

Here's a demo: https://github.com/feross/eslint-issue-3000

```
git clone git@github.com:feross/eslint-issue-3000.git
cd eslint-issue-3000
npm install
npm test
```

Your test case here (https://github.com/eslint/eslint/commit/c46b7a9144bea1241fd86b78a3d72abf1492ae50#diff-a28ba1a60512ed1edcdfca32d70ce897R57) added a `;` to the end, which might not be triggering the spurious error.
I tried it by removing it, still passes.

I can confirm that demo is failing (as is, without latest fix).
Edit: I also just tried it with the latest master and it's still gives the same error

I confirmed the bug using the repo now and it is also because of the semi at the end.
But if I use the same code inside unit test, it passes. :scream:
Hmm... Ok, now that's very interesting. Unit tests shouldn't be doing anything that would cause such behavior...

Can anyone else try it in unit test to confirm please?

use this:

``` js
{
            code:
            "while (1 < 2) console.log('hi')",
            options: [2]
        }
```
I just verified it locally, and you are correct, it's passing unittests. No idea why, but we really should investigate this.

I know why now..... ready everyone _drum roll_
AS i mentioned this issue https://github.com/eslint/espree/issues/164 where if a stement doesn't have a `;` then it make the start and end for location to be not on same line.

Now if you closely look into @feross repo and the js file in it. it has an empty line. that why.
Our unit test doesnt have that.
Ok, that makes sense. I got scared there for a second that our unittests where not testing things correctly.
